nodes.name: Heavy rainfall
nodes.desc: Wet westerly weather keeps the rainforest and moorland of western Tasmania damp for much of the year.

nodes.name: Cool maritime climate
nodes.desc: A cool, wet oceanic climate suits cool temperate rainforest, which can regenerate without large catastrophic events.

nodes.name: Acidic peat soil
nodes.desc: Buttongrass moor grows on damp, nutrient-poor, acidic peat soils in western Tasmania.

nodes.name: Fire
nodes.desc: Buttongrass moorland is adapted to regular burning, and Aboriginal burning shaped the landscape for millennia.

nodes.name: Fungi and soil microbes
nodes.desc: Break down fallen leaves, logs and carcasses, returning nutrients to the soil.

nodes.name: Myrtle beech
nodes.desc: The main canopy tree of Tasmania's cool temperate rainforest, sharing the canopy with sassafras, leatherwood and conifers.

nodes.name: Soft tree fern
nodes.desc: A tree fern that forms an open, park-like understorey in many rainforest stands.

nodes.name: Buttongrass
nodes.desc: The dominant plant of Tasmania's moorlands. Its rhizomes are eaten by burrowing crayfish, and the community is adapted to burning.

nodes.name: Silver wattle
nodes.desc: A wattle that colonises gaps and burnt ground at forest edges; black cockatoos are recorded eating its seeds.

nodes.name: Tasmanian pademelon
nodes.desc: A small wallaby that rests in thick cover by day and feeds on grass and shoots in open ground near the forest edge after dark.

nodes.name: Common wombat
nodes.desc: A burrowing grazer of grass and other plants. Its tunnels are used by many other animals and its digging turns over the soil.

nodes.name: Red-necked wallaby
nodes.desc: A grazing wallaby of open forest and heath, preyed on by devils, quolls and eagles.

nodes.name: Common brushtail possum
nodes.desc: A nocturnal, tree-dwelling marsupial that eats leaves and other plant matter, and is a frequent prey of quolls and eagles.

nodes.name: Yellow-tailed black cockatoo
nodes.desc: A large cockatoo that feeds on seeds, including those of silver wattle.

nodes.name: Burrowing crayfish
nodes.desc: Lives in burrows on moorland and eats buttongrass rhizomes; its burrows aerate the peat.

nodes.name: Forest raven
nodes.desc: The most-recorded bird near the site. It feeds on carrion such as dead wallabies and pademelons.

nodes.name: Eastern quoll
nodes.desc: A small spotted marsupial carnivore that hunts possums and smaller wallabies and takes carrion.

nodes.name: Feral cat
nodes.desc: An introduced predator recorded in the area that kills pademelons, possums and many small animals.

nodes.name: Tasmanian devil
nodes.desc: The world's largest surviving marsupial carnivore, mainly a scavenger that favours wombats. Devil facial tumour disease has cut its numbers sharply.

nodes.name: Spotted-tailed quoll
nodes.desc: Tasmania's top hunting mammal, living in rainforest and wet forest and taking possums, pademelons, wombats and crayfish.

nodes.name: Tasmanian wedge-tailed eagle
nodes.desc: A large endangered eagle that takes wallabies, possums and rabbits, and feeds on carrion in winter.
